Summary: Coordinate first response, diagnosis, escalation, and customer communication with explicit safe-refusal paths, artifact inputs, and emergency-governance notes.
ValueStatement: Shorten blocked time and preserve trust under ambiguity.
InterfaceContractSummary: Customer-facing response depends on reliable diagnosis and explicit decision rights.
GovernanceNotes: Critical escalations require approval notes and trust-aware evidence handling.
ChangeSummary: Refreshed to preserve the current concise baseline scenario while enriching diagnostic, approval, and mitigation discipline around the same three-step spine.
GovernancePolicySummary: Emergency paths stay bounded by approval, journaling, and evidence controls.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Policy decisions stay explicit and reviewable.
OperatingModeSummary: Emergency operating mode is explicitly bounded by governance rules.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Seed pack models refusal, blocking, and artifact trust scenarios.
Metrics: Median time from acknowledgement to diagnosis evidence pack.
Approvals executed with explicit mitigation rationale and rollback framing.
Percentage of incidents triaged with explicit severity and responders.
Rate of false-positive incidents safely refused without follow-on churn.
Post-incident findings caused by weak diagnosis evidence or approval discipline.
Risks: Triage proceeding with vague severity or impact framing.
Emergency changes executed without explicit approval.
Customer-impact communication drifting away from technical facts.
TailoringRules: Low-signal incidents may stop after respond with an explicit safe refusal or downgrade.
Major incidents may branch into a richer command-and-communications scenario after escalation.
If mitigation changes production state, approval remains mandatory even when the same person also owns technical response.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Turn an incoming operational signal into a structured incident response posture with explicit severity, owners, and first actions.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A disciplined incident responder who can rapidly stabilize coordination without inventing unsupported conclusions.
RoleUsages.Notes: Initial incident coordinator for severity framing and first containment path selection.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Investigate the technical fault path, propose mitigation, and execute or coordinate the change needed to restore service.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A hands-on technical responder who can diagnose the active failure mode and work with governance roles under time pressure.
RoleUsages.Notes: Primary technical owner for diagnosis, mitigation, and restoration work.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Make the accountable go / no-go decision when an incident response path requires explicit approval beyond responder discretion.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A decision owner trusted to balance restoration urgency, risk, customer impact, and evidence quality during incidents.
RoleUsages.Notes: Explicit governance decision owner for risky mitigations and escalated incident actions.

Steps.Title: Acknowledge and classify incident
Steps.Subtitle: First response and safe-refusal posture
Steps.Notes: Capture the incoming alert, classify probable severity, and establish the initial response owner.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Inbound alert, customer impact, and available evidence.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Triage lead may safely refuse malformed or irrelevant incidents.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not let an ambiguous incoming signal bypass typed acknowledgement and classification.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Another triage lead may take over without invalidating the process.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Incident triage note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for diagnosis, approval escalation, and post-incident timeline reconstruction.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture triggering signal, user impact, severity posture, responders, and first actions.

Steps.Title: Diagnose probable cause
Steps.Subtitle: Evidence-led technical assessment
Steps.Notes: Develop a diagnosis hypothesis and proposed action from logs, traces, and responder findings.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Resolver proposes action; approver decides emergency changes.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not present a mitigation as safe until evidence and rollback framing exist; block when artifact recovery is required for missing or invalid diagnosis evidence.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Resolver role may be rebound to another capable executor.
Triage lead validates communication impact before escalation.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Diagnosis evidence pack
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for approval, post-incident review, and recurring incident detection tuning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Evidence must capture source and review status.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Mitigation ready for approval
BranchOutcomes.Description: Diagnosis evidence is sufficient to send a high-risk mitigation to the approval gate.

Steps.Title: Approve escalation path
Steps.Subtitle: Emergency decision gate
Steps.Notes: Approve, block, or refuse the proposed escalation or emergency change path.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not execute high-risk mitigation without explicit approval and rollback framing; block when artifact recovery is required for missing or invalid escalation approval evidence.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Escalation approval always belongs to the current approver role holder.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Escalation approval record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for audit, post-incident review, and emergency change governance tuning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Emergency change approvals must keep explicit rationale.

LocalRoles.Summary: Evidence-preservation specialist for incident reconstruction, root-cause support, and post-incident proof.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Protect and structure the evidence required to understand what happened without obstructing urgent containment.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A technically skilled analyst focused on logs, traces, timeline reconstruction, and evidence integrity.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Evidence-preservation specialist for incident reconstruction, root-cause support, and post-incident proof.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior reliability, security, or forensic analysis
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to capture and correlate logs, traces, metrics, and operator notes into a coherent timeline.
Knowledge of evidence preservation, time-source accuracy, and contamination risk.
Understanding of what evidence is lost when containment actions are taken too early or opaquely.
Ability to support root-cause analysis without presenting speculation as fact.
Knowledge of access-control and sensitivity constraints on incident evidence.
Ability to package evidence so later review is faster and less ambiguous.
ExperienceRequirements: Has reconstructed an outage or security-relevant event from fragmented telemetry.
Has collaborated with responders to preserve evidence during active containment.
Has written or supported root-cause or timeline documentation.
Has worked with sensitive or customer-impacting incident data responsibly.
Has contributed to corrective-action definition based on evidence, not hunches.
DecisionRights: Define minimum evidence-capture requirements before destructive containment steps.
Escalate when evidence quality is insufficient for reliable root-cause analysis.
Approve timeline completeness for post-incident review.
Enforce sensitivity handling on incident evidence artifacts.
CollaborationExpectations: Work with incident commander and platform/security specialists in real time.
Document what is known, suspected, and disproven distinctly.
Support the scribe/communications path with verified facts.
Help convert findings into corrective actions with clear causal logic.
AntiPatterns: Optimizing for perfect evidence while the incident worsens.
Losing provenance of manually captured notes or screenshots.
Mixing speculation with verified fact in official timelines.
Storing sensitive evidence in the wrong access domain.
FitnessEvidence: Timelines accepted in post-incident review.
Evidence packs with preserved provenance.
Root-cause records improved by the analyst’s structured input.
Reduction in repeated 'we don’t know what happened' incidents.

LocalRoles.Summary: Structured recorder for live decisions, assignments, and status changes during incident response.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Preserve a reliable operational memory of what was decided, by whom, and when, so responders can focus without losing traceability.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A disciplined operator dedicated to live note-taking, timeline hygiene, and decision capture.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Structured recorder for live decisions, assignments, and status changes during incident response.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Experienced support, operations, or PMO contributor
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to capture decisions, owners, timestamps, and open actions accurately in fast-moving situations.
Knowledge of incident cadence, meeting hygiene, and what details are worth preserving.
Understanding of the difference between claimed status and confirmed status.
Ability to keep notes structured enough for later forensic and retrospective use.
Knowledge of confidentiality and audience boundaries for incident notes.
Ability to prompt for missing ownership or unclear decisions without disrupting flow.
ExperienceRequirements: Has supported live incident bridges, war rooms, or rapid-response coordination.
Has maintained accurate action logs or timelines under pressure.
Has turned raw live notes into usable post-incident documentation.
Has worked with executives or technical leaders in time-critical meetings.
Has enforced discipline around owner/time/next-step capture.
DecisionRights: Require explicit owner and due time when decisions are made.
Escalate when the response lacks a clear action log.
Control the official incident note set and versioning.
Flag contradictions between successive status statements.
CollaborationExpectations: Work beside the incident commander without becoming a bottleneck.
Coordinate with forensics analyst on timeline integrity.
Provide communications roles with accurate, approved status inputs.
Hand off clean notes for the post-incident review.
AntiPatterns: Trying to solve the incident instead of preserving decision quality.
Capturing minutes without owners or timestamps.
Editing history to make the response look cleaner after the fact.
Publishing notes to the wrong audience.
FitnessEvidence: High-quality incident notes consumed after the event.
Post-incident reviews that rely on the scribe record confidently.
Evidence of improved action follow-through due to disciplined logging.
Trust from incident leaders in the scribe’s accuracy.

LocalRoles.Summary: Initial incident coordinator for severity framing, responder mobilization, and first containment path selection.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Turn an incoming operational signal into a structured incident response posture with explicit severity, owners, and first actions.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A disciplined incident responder who can rapidly stabilize coordination without inventing unsupported conclusions.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Initial incident coordinator for severity framing and first containment path selection.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior support lead, site reliability engineer, or incident coordinator
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to run time-critical coordination while maintaining factual discipline.
Knowledge of incident severity frameworks, escalation protocols, and communication cadence.
Understanding of containment, rollback, degraded-mode, and forensic preservation trade-offs.
Ability to identify when a technical thread requires a business or communications decision.
Knowledge of stakeholder management under pressure, including executives and customers.
Ability to prevent chaos by assigning explicit owners and decision deadlines.
ExperienceRequirements: Has led or co-led a real production incident or equivalent crisis response.
Has coordinated technical, support, and communications workstreams simultaneously.
Has made containment decisions under uncertainty and documented the rationale.
Has facilitated post-incident review and follow-through on corrective actions.
Has dealt with high-pressure stakeholder escalation without losing factual discipline.
DecisionRights: Set incident cadence, priorities, and escalation thresholds.
Approve containment direction and stop uncoordinated interventions.
Escalate customer, legal, or executive impact when the incident crosses agreed thresholds.
Own the decision to move from active response to learning and recovery mode.
CollaborationExpectations: Coordinate specialists without micromanaging their technical work.
Keep product/service owners aware of impact and likely decision windows.
Work with communications roles so outward messaging tracks technical reality.
Protect scribe and forensic roles so evidence is not lost under pressure.
AntiPatterns: Acting as the loudest technical contributor instead of the coordinator.
Allowing parallel unapproved fixes that worsen the incident.
Optimizing for speed at the cost of evidence preservation when that evidence is needed.
Declaring the incident done before ownership of follow-through is clear.
FitnessEvidence: Incident command logs showing explicit ownership and decision timing.
Retrospectives that attribute improved containment or coordination to the role holder.
Evidence of calm, factual stakeholder communication under pressure.
Corrective actions actually delivered after incidents the role owned.

LocalRoles.Summary: Primary technical owner for diagnosis, mitigation, and restoration work inside an active incident.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Investigate the technical fault path, propose mitigation, and execute or coordinate the change needed to restore service.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A hands-on technical responder who can diagnose the active failure mode and work with governance roles under time pressure.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Primary technical owner for diagnosis, mitigation, and restoration work.
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to manage CI/CD pipelines, deployment automation, environment controls, and configuration safety.
Knowledge of secrets, identity, access, and least-privilege controls in build and deployment systems.
Understanding of observability stacks, alerting, rollout telemetry, and rollback triggers.
Ability to assess infrastructure dependencies, schema changes, and environment drift.
Knowledge of reproducible builds, provenance, and artifact integrity signals.
Ability to guide teams on what must change in delivery mechanics before code is releasable.
ExperienceRequirements: Has built or maintained deployment pipelines for production software.
Has executed or supported releases, rollback, and incident containment in live environments.
Has debugged environment-specific failures that blocked otherwise correct code.
Has implemented monitoring or telemetry needed for safe rollout decisions.
Has worked with security and compliance requirements around platform access and evidence retention.
DecisionRights: Approve or block platform readiness for build and deployment activities.
Require environment or observability changes before risky releases.
Escalate when release assumptions depend on unstable platform conditions.
Choose rollout mechanics within the approved operational policy.
CollaborationExpectations: Collaborate with engineers to make deployment and observability requirements explicit early.
Coordinate with release approvers on rollout and rollback realism.
Work with security on platform trust and access-control expectations.
Support incident response with high-fidelity operational evidence.
AntiPatterns: Treating platform concerns as someone else's problem until release day.
Automating blindly without observability or rollback triggers.
Using production-specific knowledge that is not documented or transferable.
Assuming a successful build implies a safe deployment.
FitnessEvidence: Reliable deployment and rollback exercises.
Evidence of improved pipeline stability or reduced release friction.
Clear platform runbooks or operational notes owned by the role holder.
Strong trust from delivery teams in platform signals and readiness calls.

LocalRoles.Summary: Explicit governance decision owner for escalated incident actions, risky mitigations, or customer-impacting restoration choices.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Make the accountable go / no-go decision when an incident response path requires explicit approval beyond responder discretion.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A decision owner trusted to balance restoration urgency, risk, customer impact, and evidence quality during incidents.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Explicit governance decision owner for risky mitigations and escalated incident actions.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior operations manager or delegated executive owner
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to judge release readiness from business, technical, QA, security, and operational signals together.
Knowledge of rollback strategy, deployment controls, maintenance windows, and support readiness.
Understanding of incident escalation, customer communication, and operational ownership after go-live.
Ability to distinguish reversible risk from unacceptable irreversible exposure.
Knowledge of auditability and approval traceability expectations.
Ability to enforce a no-go decision when evidence quality is not credible.
ExperienceRequirements: Has owned or chaired at least one production release or change approval forum.
Has made go/no-go decisions under time pressure with incomplete but structured evidence.
Has handled release rollback or controlled stop conditions in real environments.
Has coordinated post-release monitoring and support readiness across teams.
Has worked through customer-impacting defects or incidents after approving a release.
DecisionRights: Authorize or reject production deployment.
Require explicit rollback and monitoring coverage before release.
Escalate to executive authority when residual risk exceeds delegated tolerance.
Freeze release progression when mandatory gates remain unresolved.
CollaborationExpectations: Consume input from product, QA, security, platform, and service owners before deciding.
State release decision rationale in explicit, reviewable language.
Trigger support and communications readiness when customer impact is plausible.
Capture follow-up actions for conditions attached to release approval.
AntiPatterns: Approving because teams appear confident without checking the evidence.
Conflating deployment success with business-release success.
Ignoring rollback realism because the change is 'small'.
Treating approval as ceremonial rather than consequential.
FitnessEvidence: Signed release decisions with clear rationale and conditions.
Examples of stopped or delayed releases where later evidence justified the decision.
Operational metrics showing disciplined release governance.
Trust from delivery teams that the role is demanding but consistent.

LocalArtifacts.Summary: Explicit containment plan selected during the incident, including decision trade-offs and monitoring expectations.
LocalArtifacts.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for incident execution, post-incident review, and improvement planning only.
LocalArtifacts.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must distinguish immediate containment from long-term fix.

LocalArtifacts.Summary: Decision note that explains the chosen immediate containment or mitigation path during incident response.
LocalArtifacts.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for diagnosis, approval escalation, and post-incident review.
LocalArtifacts.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must describe the chosen containment path, expected effect, and residual uncertainty.

LocalChecklists.Summary: Checklist to keep the incident bridge factual, owned, and time-bounded under pressure.
LocalChecklists.EntryCriteria: Incident bridge is active and multiple people are contributing.
LocalChecklists.ExitCriteria: Decision owner, next checkpoint, and live action log quality remain intact.
Checks: Current severity and impact are stated at the top of the bridge.
Every action has an owner and next update time.

LocalChecklists.Summary: Keeps incident diagnosis evidence-led and protects against destructive or unsupported mitigation guesses.
LocalChecklists.EntryCriteria: The incident has been triaged and diagnosis is underway.
LocalChecklists.ExitCriteria: Diagnosis notes distinguish hypotheses, evidence, and approved mitigation clearly.
Checks: Potentially destructive mitigations are flagged for approval.
Rollback or reversal options are noted where applicable.

LocalValidations.Summary: Confirms the response has preserved enough evidence for later root-cause understanding.
LocalValidations.PassCriteria: Critical logs, traces, screenshots, and operator notes have been captured or intentionally sacrificed with rationale.
LocalValidations.FailCriteria: Destructive containment or cleanup occurred without preserving key evidence.
LocalValidations.EscalationRule: Escalate to incident commander and compliance/security stakeholders as appropriate.

LocalValidations.Summary: Prevents high-risk incident mitigation from proceeding without explicit approval when required.
LocalValidations.PassCriteria: Risky mitigation steps have an approval record naming owner, conditions, and rollback trigger.
LocalValidations.FailCriteria: High-risk mitigation would proceed without explicit approval or rollback framing.
LocalValidations.EscalationRule: Pause the mitigation and escalate to the approver.

LocalPrompts.Summary: Prompt scaffold for concise executive updates during an active incident.
RefusalConditions: Refuse to include unverified root-cause claims in the executive summary.

LocalPrompts.Summary: Generates a structured list of mitigation options with evidence, risk, and rollback framing.
RequiredInputs: Known service architecture or dependency context.
RefusalConditions: Do not invent root cause certainty.
Refuse when available evidence is too weak to rank mitigation options meaningfully.
